labeling_note: The firm must transport the injured insured to a treatment facility approved by the Corporation, report reportable injuries to the nearest police station within 48 hours, and notify the Corporation in writing with the initial medical report within 14 working days. If it fails to report to the Corporation on time it must cover 15% of the injured person's treatment expenses.

question_text: I cannot work while I recover from an injury I got at work. Will I still be paid, and how much?
labeling_note: A daily allowance equal to 75% of the daily wage on which contributions were calculated at the date of injury, paid for the days spent under treatment at an approved centre or at home per a Medical Reference decision. It continues while the injured is unable to resume work, or until permanent disability is confirmed or death occurs.

question_text: If someone is killed or left permanently unable to work because of an accident at work, what money is paid and how is the amount worked out?
labeling_note:
Article 30 distinguishes four cases.
(a) Death due to work injury: survivor beneficiaries receive a pension of 75% of the wage used to calculate contributions at the date of injury, accruing from the start of the month in which death occurs.
(b) Total permanent work-related disability: a monthly pension of 75% of that same wage, accruing from the date the Medical Reference confirms the condition has stabilised, increased by 25% if the Medical Reference decides the injured needs assistance to perform daily life tasks -- that increase capped at the approved minimum wage under the Labor Law.
(c) Partial permanent disability of 30% or more: a monthly pension equal to the disability percentage applied to the paragraph (b) total-disability pension, from the date of health stability.
(d) Partial permanent disability below 30%: a lump sum equal to that proportion of the paragraph (b) amount, multiplied by 36 months.

question_text: Can someone lose their right to injury money because of the way they behaved?
labeling_note: Entitlement to the daily allowance and the lump sum compensation lapses if the injury resulted from a deliberate act; from being under the influence of alcohol, narcotics, psychotropic substances or dangerous drugs; or from failing to comply with announced mandatory treatment or occupational safety instructions where that non-compliance was the main cause of the injury, a significant factor in it, or delayed recovery. These must be confirmed by an investigation carried out or approved by the Corporation.

question_text: Can I also sue my employer for more than what social security pays me for my injury?
labeling_note: No. Neither the injured nor their heirs or survivor beneficiaries may recourse to the firm for work-injury compensation beyond what this Law provides -- unless the injury resulted from a serious mistake on the part of the firm.

question_text: Can I stop working before the normal retirement age, and how would my pension be worked out?
labeling_note:
Article 64 provides several routes, all on the insured's request after service ends for any reason.
(a) Age 50 or above with at least 252 actual contributions for a male or 228 for a female; or 300 actual contributions at age 45.
(b) Transitional cases for those who had reached a given age before the Law took effect -- for example age 46 with at least 228 actual contributions (male) or 192 (female) for someone who had turned 44 before that date, with equivalent steps at ages 47 and 48.
(c) Hazardous professions: age 45 or above with at least 216 actual contributions (male) or 180 (female), where the insured worked in that profession for at least 60 contributions in the preceding 10 years; the firm pays an extra 1% of wage.
(d) Calculation: 2.5% per contribution year on the first JOD 1500 of the average monthly wage over the last 60 contributions and 2% on the remainder, then reduced by age according to appended Table 5, with dependant increases of 12% for the first dependant (JOD 10-100) and 6% each for the second and third (JOD 10-25).
(h) For anyone first covered after the amended Law took effect: male age 55 with at least 252 actual contributions, female age 52 with at least 228.

question_text: What time off can I take during the year, and which of it is paid?
labeling_note:
Four articles combine.
Article 61 -- annual leave: 14 days on full pay per year of service, rising to 21 days once the worker completes five consecutive years with the same employer; official holidays, religious holidays and weekends are not counted against it; a worker with less than a full year gets paid leave in proportion to time worked; leave may be deferred by agreement to the immediately following year, the employer may not refuse a request to take it, and refusal for two years costs the employer a JOD 100 fine plus a cash substitute.
Article 65 -- sick leave: 14 days per year on full pay on a report from the institution's approved physician, renewable for a further 14 days on full pay if the worker is hospitalised.
Article 66 -- additional leaves: 14 paid days per year for an approved labour training course, or to perform the Hajj (requiring five continuous years with the employer, granted once in the service period); four months UNPAID for study at an officially recognised university, institute or college; and three days paid paternity leave.
Article 70 -- maternity leave: ten weeks fully paid in total before and after childbirth, of which not less than six weeks must fall after the birth.

question_text: When can an employer dismiss someone on the spot, with no warning at all?
labeling_note:
Article 28 lists nine cases:
1. Impersonating another person or identity, or providing forged certificates or documents to gain benefit or harm others.
2. Failing to fulfil the obligations under the employment contract.
3. Committing a mistake causing serious financial loss to the employer, provided the employer notifies the competent authority within five days of learning of it.
4. Violating the institution's internal regulations, including work and worker safety conditions, after two written warnings.
5. Absence without legitimate reason for more than twenty separate days in one year, or more than ten consecutive days, preceded by a written warning sent by registered mail and published once in a local daily newspaper.
6. Disclosing work secrets.
7. Being found guilty by conclusive judicial verdict of a felony or misdemeanour contravening honour and public morals.
8. Being found at work drunk or under the influence of a narcotic or psychotropic substance, or committing an act violating public morals in the workplace.
9. Assaulting the employer, the director in charge, a superior, another worker or any other person during or because of work, by beating or degradation.

question_text: When must my wages reach me, and what is my employer allowed to take out of them?
labeling_note:
Two articles combine.
Article 46: wages and overtime must be paid within seven days of the date of maturity, and the employer may not deduct any part of them except in cases permitted by law; the worker's signature on a wage register or on a receipt does not waive their right to any further amount due under law, regulation or contract. Article 47 permits deduction only in seven cases:
1. Recovering advances paid by the employer, with each repayment instalment capped at 10% of the wage.
2. Refunding any amount paid in excess of entitlement.
3. Social security subscriptions and instalments due, and deductions required under other laws.
4. The worker's provident fund subscriptions.
5. Agreed charges for employer-provided housing and other benefits or services.
6. A debt collected in execution of a judicial verdict.
7. Amounts imposed for violating the institution's internal regulations or the work contract, or for materials or tools destroyed through the worker's negligence or mistake.

question_text: How long can I stay off work after giving birth, and do I get time during the day for breastfeeding afterwards?
labeling_note:
Two articles combine.
Article 70: ten weeks of fully paid maternity leave before and after childbirth in total, of which not less than six weeks must fall after the birth, and it is prohibited to employ her before that six-week period expires.
Article 71: after the maternity leave under Article 70 ends, the working woman has the right, within one year from the date of birth, to take one or more periods per day on full pay to breastfeed her newborn, not exceeding a total of one hour per day.

أربع مواد تتكامل.

labeling_note: No wage stated at all -- expect the 125% rate given as a percentage of the regular hourly wage. No JD figure should appear, since nothing was stated to compute one from.

labeling_note: Targets the SECOND rate in Article 59 specifically -- 150% for the weekly day off or a holiday, distinct from the 125% ordinary-overtime rate. A wrong-rate answer (125% instead of 150%) is the failure this question exists to catch.

Expect the 150% rate stated as a percentage of the normal hourly wage -- a JD figure computed by dividing 900 by some invented number of hours/days would be an ungrounded number and is the specific failure this question is designed to catch.

question_text: اشتغلت 3 سنوات عند نفس صاحب العمل، كم رصيد إجازتي السنوية؟
labeling_note: Phase 26, live-verified over real HTTP. Below the 5-year threshold, so the total is exact and unambiguous: 14 days/year x 3 years = 42 days.

labeling_note: Phase 26's live-caught bug, verbatim. Correct behaviour is to state both rates (14 and 21 days/year) and the 5-year threshold, and say plainly that a single total cannot be given without knowing when the threshold was reached.

question_text: كم النسبة التي تتحملها الشركة عن الموظف في الضمان الاجتماعي
labeling_note: The reported failure, verbatim. Employer share is the sum of four separate insurances: 59(a)(1) old-age/disability/death 11%, 24(a) work injury 2%, 42(a)(1) maternity 0.75%, 48(a) unemployment 0.5% = 14.25%. Production answered 11% citing only Article 59.

labeling_note: English form of r01. Same four articles, same 14.25% total.

labeling_note: Employee side only: 59(a)(2) 6.5% + 48(b) 1% = 7.5%. The other two insurances have no employee deduction.

question_text: هل يدفع صاحب العمل مبلغاً مقابل تغطيتي إذا تعرضت لحادث في العمل؟
labeling_note: Article 24(a): establishment pays 2%, written as 'اثنين بالمائة' in words rather than digits -- the retrieval failure this set exists to catch.

question_text: أنا موظف رجل، هل يُدفع عني شيء لتأمين الأمومة؟
labeling_note: Yes. Article 43(a) applies maternity insurance to all insured persons; 42(a)(1) charges 0.75% on the wages of all of them. Nothing is deducted from the employee -- it is employer-only. Only 'المؤمن عليها' (feminine, Articles 44/45) can draw the benefit.

question_text: لو فقدت وظيفتي، من كان يدفع تأمين التعطل، أنا أم الشركة؟
labeling_note: Both. Article 48(a) establishment 0.5%, 48(b) 1% deducted from the employee. Both written in words, not digits.

question_text: أعمل في مزرعة، ما التأمينات التي تشملني فعلياً؟
labeling_note: Article 59(d)(1): agricultural holdings are covered by work injury and maternity only, until a Council of Ministers decision extends the rest. So the employer share is 2.75%, not 14.25%.

question_text: أنا موظف في القطاع العام، كم تدفع الجهة التي أعمل بها عني؟
labeling_note: Article 72 governs the public sector separately: 2% work injury + 11% old-age, 6.5% deducted. Armed forces/security are 17/21.5/26% depending on the previous year's real growth rate.

question_text: عمري 27 سنة وهذه أول وظيفة أسجل بها، هل هناك تخفيض على ما يُدفع عني؟
labeling_note: Article 59(c)(1): private-sector establishments may reduce the 11% component for Jordanians under 30 never previously covered, by up to 50%, with ratios set by regulation.

question_text: I work for myself. If I join social security by choice, what share would I be paying?
labeling_note: Article 59(a)(3): voluntary subscribers under Article 7 pay 17.5% themselves. Commonly confused with the employer rate.

question_text: I work for a government ministry. Does this labor law apply to my job?
labeling_note: Article 3(a) excludes public servants and municipal employees from the Labour Law's coverage entirely -- their employment is governed by separate civil service rules, not this law.

question_text_statute: Does the Labour Law apply to public servants and municipal employees?
expected_behavior: The answer should state that Labour Law 1996 does NOT apply to government/municipal employees per Article 3(a), rather than answering as if standard labor law protections apply to this job.

question_text: أعمل موظفاً في وزارة حكومية. هل ينطبق علي قانون العمل هذا؟

source_article_excerpt: المادة (3): المستثنون من القانون. أ- ...تطبق أحكام هذا القانون على جميع العمال واصحاب العمل باستثناء الموظفين العامين وموظفي البلديات.

expected_behavior: يجب أن تذكر الإجابة أن قانون العمل لسنة 1996 لا ينطبق على الموظفين العامين وموظفي البلديات بموجب المادة 3(أ)، لا أن تجيب وكأن حماية قانون العمل الاعتيادية تسري على هذه الوظيفة.

question_text: I work as a housekeeper in someone's home. Am I covered by the labor law the same way as other workers?
labeling_note: Article 3(b) states domestic workers (along with agricultural workers, cooks, gardeners, and similar) are not covered by the Labour Law's ordinary provisions -- their work conditions are instead set by a separate regulation covering contracts, hours, rest, and inspection.
source_article_excerpt: b- The provisions to which agricultural workers, domestic workers, chefs, gardeners, and the like are subjected to shall be determined under a regulation issued for this purpose...
question_text_statute: Does the Labour Law's ordinary provisions cover domestic workers?
expected_behavior: The answer should state that domestic workers are excluded from the Labour Law's ordinary provisions per Article 3(b), governed instead by a separate regulation, rather than answering as if standard labor law protections apply.

question_text: أعمل خادمة منزلية في بيت أحد الأشخاص. هل أنا مشمولة بقانون العمل مثل باقي العمال؟
labeling_note: المادة 3(ب) تنص على أن العاملين في المنازل (وكذلك عمال الزراعة والطهاة والبستانيين ومن في حكمهم) لا يخضعون للأحكام الاعتيادية لقانون العمل، بل تحدد شروط عملهم بنظام منفصل يغطي العقود وساعات العمل والراحة والتفتيش.
source_article_excerpt: ب- تحدد الاحكام التي يخضع اليها عمال الزراعة والعاملون في المنازل وخدماتها وبساتينها ومن في حكمهم بمقتضى نظام يصدر لهذه الغاية...
question_text_statute: هل تسري الأحكام الاعتيادية لقانون العمل على العاملين في المنازل؟
expected_behavior: يجب أن تذكر الإجابة أن العاملين في المنازل مستثنون من الأحكام الاعتيادية لقانون العمل بموجب المادة 3(ب)، وأن عملهم يخضع لنظام منفصل، لا أن تجيب وكأن أحكام قانون العمل الاعتيادية تسري عليهم.

question_text: I'm a professional in a field not officially listed by the government yet. Does this professional work law cover me?
labeling_note: Article 3 states the Professional Work Law only applies to professions and businesses the Council of Ministers (per the Minister's recommendation) decides to include under it -- a profession not yet added is not covered by this law at all.
source_article_excerpt: Article (3): The provisions of this Law apply to professions and businesses that the Council of Ministers decides to include under this Law based on the recommendation of the Minister.
question_text_statute: Does the Professional Work Law apply to a profession the Council of Ministers has not decided to include under it?
expected_behavior: The answer should state that the Professional Work Law only covers professions the Council of Ministers has formally added, and that an unlisted profession is not covered by it at all.

question_text: أنا أعمل في مهنة لم يتم إدراجها رسمياً من قبل الحكومة بعد. هل يشملني قانون العمل المهني؟
labeling_note: المادة 3 تنص على أن قانون العمل المهني يسري فقط على المهن والمحلات التي يقرر الوزير شمولها بأحكامه -- المهنة التي لم تُدرج بعد لا يشملها هذا القانون إطلاقاً.

question_text_statute: هل يسري قانون العمل المهني على مهنة لم يقرر الوزير شمولها بأحكامه؟

question_text: Can I get a tourist visa extension while working in Jordan?
labeling_note: Visa and immigration matters are not covered by the Jordanian Labour Law, Social Security Law, or Professional Work Law. Correct behavior is to state plainly that these documents don't address this (rule 2), not to guess or answer from general knowledge.
question_text_statute: Is tourist visa extension addressed by Jordanian labor or social security legislation?
expected_behavior: The answer should plainly state that the provided legal documents do not address visa/immigration matters, rather than fabricating an answer from general knowledge.

question_text: هل يمكنني تمديد تأشيرة سياحية أثناء عملي في الأردن؟
labeling_note: مسائل التأشيرات والهجرة لا يغطيها قانون العمل الأردني ولا قانون الضمان الاجتماعي ولا قانون العمل المهني. السلوك الصحيح هو ذكر أن هذه الوثائق لا تجيب عن هذا السؤال بوضوح (القاعدة 2)، لا التخمين أو الإجابة من معرفة عامة.

question_text: I'm a freelancer and not required to join social security. Should I sign up for it voluntarily?
labeling_note: Article 7 lets certain categories (Jordanians under 60/55, persons who left the law's scope, firm owners under another mandatory scheme) join Old-Age/Disability/Death insurance voluntarily for eventual pension eligibility -- but the voluntary insured must pay BOTH the employer's and employee's full contribution shares themselves (17.5% total, per Article 59(a)(3)), plus a 1% monthly penalty for late payment. Correct behavior states both the benefit and the cost/obligation neutrally, without recommending a decision either way (rule 13) -- flagging as correct only if it doesn't push the person one way.
source_article_excerpt: Article (7) a. Each of the following categories may contribute for a voluntary old age, disability and death insurance... b. An insured who contributes voluntarily... shall pay in full the contributions payable by the firm and the insured...
question_text_statute: What are the conditions and obligations for voluntary contribution to Old-Age, Disability and Death Insurance under Article 7?
expected_behavior: The answer should state both the benefit (pension eligibility) and the cost/obligation (paying both contribution shares, 17.5% total, plus late penalties) neutrally, side by side, WITHOUT recommending whether to join or not.

question_text: أنا أعمل لحسابي الخاص ولست ملزماً بالانتساب للضمان الاجتماعي. هل يجدر بي الانتساب اختيارياً؟
labeling_note: المادة 7 تسمح لفئات معينة (الأردنيون دون سن 60/55، من خرج من نطاق تطبيق القانون، أصحاب المنشآت الخاضعون لنظام تقاعد إلزامي آخر) بالانتساب اختيارياً لتأمين الشيخوخة والعجز والوفاة لغايات استحقاق راتب تقاعد لاحقاً -- لكن المنتسب اختيارياً يدفع كامل حصتي المنشأة والمؤمن عليه معاً (17.5% إجمالاً حسب المادة 59(أ)(3))، بالإضافة إلى فائدة تأخير 1% شهرياً. السلوك الصحيح يذكر الفائدة والالتزام المالي معاً بشكل محايد دون التوصية بقرار معين (القاعدة 13).
source_article_excerpt: المادة (7) أ- يجوز لكل من الفئات التالية الانتساب بصفة اختيارية الى تأمين الشيخوخة والعجز والوفاة... ب- يؤدي المؤمن عليه الذي انتسب بصفة اختيارية... الاشتراكات التي تلتزم بها المنشأة والتي يلتزم بها المؤمن عليه كاملةً...
question_text_statute: ما هي شروط والتزامات الانتساب الاختياري لتأمين الشيخوخة والعجز والوفاة بموجب المادة 7؟
expected_behavior: يجب أن تذكر الإجابة الفائدة (استحقاق راتب تقاعد) والالتزام المالي (دفع كامل الحصتين، 17.5% إجمالاً، بالإضافة إلى فوائد التأخير) بشكل محايد وجنباً إلى جنب، دون التوصية بالانتساب من عدمه.

question_text: I'm a shift supervisor and sometimes work extra hours. Am I entitled to overtime pay?
labeling_note: Article 59 sets overtime at 125% of regular wage (150% on rest days/holidays), but Article 58 excludes anyone in a general supervisory/management role, or whose job requires travel, from the working-hours articles entirely. A supervisor's entitlement genuinely depends on whether their role counts as 'general supervision' -- a fact this question doesn't establish, so the correct behavior asks or states the rates as conditional (matching compute_overtime's Article 58 guardrail from Phase 28), not a flat yes/no.
source_article_excerpt: Article 58: ...do not apply to individuals tasked with the general supervision or management of the institution... Article 59: ...compensation for each overtime hour not less than (125%) of their regular wage.
question_text_statute: Does the overtime entitlement in Article 59 apply to a worker excluded under Article 58's general supervision exception?

question_text: أنا مشرف نوبة عمل وأعمل أحياناً ساعات إضافية. هل أستحق أجر العمل الإضافي؟
labeling_note: المادة 59 تحدد أجر العمل الإضافي بـ 125% من الأجر المعتاد (150% في أيام العطل والأعياد)، لكن المادة 58 تستثني من تُناط به مهام الإشراف العام أو الإدارة، أو من تتطلب طبيعة عمله السفر، من أحكام مواد ساعات العمل بالكامل. استحقاق المشرف يعتمد فعلياً على ما إذا كان دوره يُعد 'إشرافاً عاماً' -- وهي حقيقة لا يوضحها السؤال، فالسلوك الصحيح يسأل أو يذكر النسب كشرط معلّق، لا إجابة قاطعة بنعم أو لا.
source_article_excerpt: المادة 58: لا تسري أحكام المواد المتعلقة بساعات العمل... على الأشخاص الذين يتولون مهام الإشراف العام على المؤسسة أو إدارتها... المادة 59: أجراً لا يقل عن 125% من أجره المعتاد.
question_text_statute: هل ينطبق استحقاق العمل الإضافي في المادة 59 على عامل مستثنى بموجب استثناء الإشراف العام في المادة 58؟

question_text: If I get hurt on the job, who actually pays me -- my employer directly, or social security?
labeling_note: This depends entirely on Article 86: the Labour Law's employer-paid injury compensation (Articles 90-92) only applies to workers NOT subject to the Social Security Law. If the worker IS covered by Social Security, SSL Article 25/30 provisions apply instead and the Corporation pays, not the employer directly. A correct answer names this governing condition and both possible payers rather than picking one. [Grading note: switched from citation-check to behavior-judge -- a correct answer names the substantive payer articles (SSL 29/30, labor96 88/90/92), not the scoping clause Article 86 itself, so citation-matching against Article 86 alone was the wrong test.]
source_article_excerpt: Article 86 Application of work injuries: The provisions of this chapter related to work injuries and occupational diseases shall apply to workers who are not subject to the provisions of the applicable Social Security Law.
question_text_statute: Under Article 86, does the employer or the Social Security Corporation pay work-injury compensation?
expected_behavior: The answer should name the governing condition (whether the worker is covered by Social Security) and correctly identify BOTH possible payers -- the Social Security Corporation if covered, the employer directly (Labour Law compensation) if not -- rather than naming only one payer unconditionally.

question_text: إذا أصبت في عملي، من الذي يدفع لي فعلياً -- صاحب العمل مباشرة أم الضمان الاجتماعي؟
labeling_note: يعتمد الجواب كلياً على المادة 86: تعويض إصابة العمل الذي يدفعه صاحب العمل (المواد 90-92 من قانون العمل) لا ينطبق إلا على العمال غير الخاضعين لقانون الضمان الاجتماعي. أما إذا كان العامل مشمولاً بالضمان الاجتماعي، فتطبق أحكام المادة 25/30 من قانون الضمان الاجتماعي بدلاً من ذلك، وتدفع المؤسسة لا صاحب العمل مباشرة. الإجابة الصحيحة تذكر هذا الشرط الحاكم وكلا الجهتين الممكنتين بدلاً من اختيار واحدة. [Grading note: switched from citation-check to behavior-judge -- a correct answer names the substantive payer articles (SSL 29/30, labor96 88/90/92), not the scoping clause Article 86 itself, so citation-matching against Article 86 alone was the wrong test.]
source_article_excerpt: المادة 86: تطبيق اصابات العمل. تطبق احكام هذا الفصل المتعلقة باصابات العمل وامراض المهنة على العمال الذين لا تسري عليهم احكام قانون الضمان الاجتماعي المعمول به.
question_text_statute: بموجب المادة 86، هل يدفع صاحب العمل أم مؤسسة الضمان الاجتماعي تعويض إصابة العمل؟
expected_behavior: يجب أن تذكر الإجابة الشرط الحاكم (ما إذا كان العامل مشمولاً بالضمان الاجتماعي) وأن تحدد بشكل صحيح كلا الجهتين الممكنتين للدفع -- مؤسسة الضمان الاجتماعي إن كان مشمولاً، أو صاحب العمل مباشرة (تعويض قانون العمل) إن لم يكن كذلك -- بدلاً من ذكر جهة واحدة فقط دون شرط.

question_text: I already receive a work-injury disability pension. Can I also receive my regular retirement pension at the same time?
labeling_note: This is about combining TWO PENSIONS, not wages, so Article 85(b) governs -- not Article 40, which is specifically about combining a disability pension with WAGES from a job, not with another pension. Article 85(b) allows combining, capped at 3x the minimum pension amount, with only the higher pension paid if the combined total would exceed that. This tests the Article 40-vs-85 disambiguation (Phase 35) in the OTHER direction from prior tests: the model must correctly pick Article 85 here rather than defaulting to Article 40 just because both are always retrieved together.
source_article_excerpt: Article (85) b. The partial permanent work-related disability pensioner and the total permanent work-related disability pensioner may combine between his/her pension and any other Retirement Pension or Disability Pension allocated to him/her...provided that the amount of these pensions is no more than (3) times the minimum limit...
question_text_statute: Under Article 85(b), can a work-injury disability pension be combined with a retirement pension, and what is the cap?

question_text: أتقاضى راتب اعتلال عجز إصابة عمل. هل يمكنني أن أتقاضى راتب التقاعد العادي في نفس الوقت أيضاً؟

source_article_excerpt: المادة (85) ب- يحق لصاحب راتب اعتلال العجز الجزئي الإصابي الدائم أو صاحب راتب اعتلال العجز الكلي الإصابي الدائم الجمع بين هذا الراتب وأي راتب تقاعد أو راتب اعتلال يخصص له... شريطة أن لا يزيد مجموعهما على ثلاثة أمثال الحد الأدنى...
question_text_statute: بموجب المادة 85(ب)، هل يمكن الجمع بين راتب اعتلال إصابة عمل وراتب تقاعد، وما هو السقف؟
